### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c31db44947483ea7a70de1fc3c7d8466174f3606` — the merge of head `b5edf8ea83f244d78f1ff1e94602b50f0cf1cde3` into base `cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c31db44947483ea7a70de1fc3c7d8466174f3606 && git checkout c31db44947483ea7a70de1fc3c7d8466174f3606
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd b5edf8ea83f244d78f1ff1e94602b50f0cf1cde3 && git checkout -B drift-repro cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd && git merge --no-ff b5edf8ea83f244d78f1ff1e94602b50f0cf1cde3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cf478ea3398e90e97e73f421fd7f0842a6bd04bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review for card #30851 (follow-up to #30213 ruling A, PR #30800 records 6676544432 / 6677397495) · schema face (`packages/spec/src/**` hit) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, brief per `record-recognisers --template --paths …`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b5edf8ea83f244d78f1ff1e94602b50f0cf1cde3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts (`deciderSegmentContext`, `decisionImpersonatorOf`, the re-suspend persist site), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`resolveDecisionSegmentContext` docblock), packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (`RunDataContext.impersonatedBy`, `resolveRunDataContext`, read), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (`decideAndResume`, `actingUserId`, `impersonatorOf`, `serviceResume`, `resumeRecordedOutcome`, `journalStrandedContinuation`, `resolveRecordedContinuation`, `continueRestoredRun`, the recall journal site, the SLA sweep), packages/rest/src/approvals-routes.ts (decision route, read), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (session arm, read), packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts (provenance projection, read), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-actor-attribution.ts (`AttributedAuthActor`, `AuthActorResolver`, `resolveAttributedActor`, `attributedActorOf`, `runAttributedToUser`, `authSystemWriteContext`), auth-manager-actor-guards.ts (`resolveActor`), auth-manager-before-hook.ts, auth-manager.ts (signature only), auth-plugin.ts (`gateAdmin` and the six `runAttributedToUser` call sites), platform-admin-gate.ts (`PlatformAdminActor.impersonatedBy`), objectql-adapter.ts (`withSystemContext`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts (export star, read), packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json and export-origins/contracts.json (read), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (level rule, read), .changeset/30851-impersonation-identity-and-decider.md, and the four pin files the diff adds to.

The diff is 16 files, +484/-48 against merge-base `e603385f`. Nothing the hit promises was taken on the PR body's word: each claim below was read in the cited code at `b5edf8ea`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`ResumeSignal.impersonatedBy` (new, optional) — right.** The one reader is `deciderSegmentContext` (run-resume.ts L320–364). It computes `decider` from `signal.resumedBy` only when `signal[RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE] === true` and returns the persisted context before `decisionImpersonatorOf(signal)` is ever read when there is no decider (L326–333). So the member is honoured exactly as `resumedBy` is: beside a decider, under the in-process symbol. `RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE` is `Symbol.for(…)` (automation-service.ts L837), which no JSON body can carry. The producer is `ApprovalService.decideAndResume` (approval-service.ts L5649–5666): `impersonatorOf(context)` reads `ExecutionContext.impersonatedBy` off the decision request's context, trimmed, and only when `actingUserId(context)` names a decider; nothing reads `input`. The REST decision route (approvals-routes.ts L480–495) passes `resolveExecCtx(…)` as the context and the body only as `input`; `ExecutionContext.impersonatedBy` has one writer, the session arm of `resolveAuthzContextInScope` (resolve-authz-context.ts L643–644), unchanged by this PR. The SLA sweep passes `SYSTEM_CTX` (L8270), so an auto-decision names neither decider nor administrator. The action-link path (L6979) has no session and so carries none, by construction.
- **`AutomationContext.impersonatedBy` docblock — right.** "An approval decision replaces it for the decider's segment with the decision's own `ResumeSignal.impersonatedBy` … absent when the decider acted in their own name, never the stamp of the write that started the run": the self-decider branch (L334–340) strips or replaces the trigger-time stamp, the switched branch (L356–357) deletes it and then sets the decision's value. The segment context is what the next pause persists (run-resume.ts re-suspend site, `context` not `run.context`), so a cold resume after a restart continues with the decision's stamp, as the engine docblock says. `resolveRunDataContext` (runtime-identity.ts L344–346) carries the trimmed value on both `runAs` arms into the kernel `ExecutionContext`, and objectql's plumbing (engine-execution-plumbing.ts L145–151) projects it to `provenance`, which the audit writer stamps. The "as on the decision itself" clause holds too: the verdict mirror writes with the same request context.
- **`resolveAttributedActor` / `AttributedAuthActor` (new plugin-auth exports, published through `export *` in index.ts L108) — right.** `attributedActorOf` answers `undefined` without a user id, so an administrator alone never attributes anything; `impersonatedBy` is answered only as a non-blank trimmed string. `resolveAttributedUserId` is now a projection, so no second resolver shape exists. The resolver the before-hook installs reads `resolveActor(ctx)`, whose `impersonatorOn` reads `session.impersonatedBy ?? session.impersonated_by` off the `getSessionFromCtx` read or the token-fallback session row (auth-manager-actor-guards.ts L134–136, L147, L193): the session, never the body. `AuthActorResolver` widened to accept the object form while a bare string keeps its meaning.
- **`PlatformAdminActor.impersonatedBy` (optional) — right.** Set only by the route's `gateAdmin` closure (auth-plugin.ts L3612–3615) from `session.session.impersonatedBy`, after `judgePlatformAdmin` has already ruled; the verdict does not read it. `runAttributedToUser` accepts the actor object and sets the resolver to `{ userId: actor.id, impersonatedBy }`; `authSystemWriteContext` spreads it beside `attributedUserId` with `isSystem: true` and no `userId`. `withSystemContext` now builds its write context from that same function, so the adapter, the membership reconciler and the admin routes carry one shape.
- **Attribution-only, verified by enumeration.** Every non-test reader of `impersonatedBy` at `b5edf8ea` is a producer (authz session arm, plugin-auth session reads), a carrier (automation context, run data context, provenance, journal) or the audit writers (`audit-writers.ts`, `action-invocation-audit.ts`). No permission evaluator, grant seeding or `isSystem` decision reads it. `userId`, `attributedUserId`, `permissions`, `positions` and `posture` move exactly as before this PR.

### ② Semver level

One changeset, four packages at `patch`, carrying `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, both line-initial, matching the PR body. **Patch is right.** This repo's rule is the maintainer's ruling A on #25105 as mechanized in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (the "Ruling A: the level follows the protocol" block) and stated in AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`"; `Clause-②` keeps its meaning (it is what put this PR on the contract-review face) and lost its level coupling. `none` is right: no authorable key, value or type moves; `ResumeSignal` is a TS interface, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` records exports by name only (the breadth half of ADR-0059) and already lists it through `export-origins/contracts.json`, so no committed artifact is stale. `Check Changeset` is green on this head. No minor is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Surface beyond the named files (engine.ts docblock; auth-manager.ts, auth-plugin.ts, auth-manager-before-hook.ts, auth-manager-actor-guards.ts, objectql-adapter.ts, platform-admin-gate.ts) — accepted.** The claim's file surface is `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/**` for item 1, which covers every plugin-auth file; the engine.ts hunk is the docblock of the method whose body run-resume.ts carries, and a body change with its contract left stale would be the finding. Each extra plugin-auth hunk is the same seam (session to resolver to write context) and none is independent work.
- **Open PR #30717 edits auth-manager.ts / auth-plugin.ts — no overlap.** Its hunks sit at auth-manager.ts L1210–2190 and auth-plugin.ts L42–3300; this PR's are at auth-manager.ts L4936 and auth-plugin.ts L3605 and after. Textually disjoint and semantically unrelated (allowed IP ranges). Whichever lands second merges clean; the dev's commitment to merge `origin/main` after it stands.
- **Clause-② re-derived from provisional `no` to `yes (widening)` — right.** The claim's `no` was a guess at attribution-only metadata; the diff adds a public spec member, two plugin-auth exports and an optional actor field, which is a widening of a published public surface by the AGENTS.md definition. The re-derivation is the dev's duty and was done; it is what put this PR on the contract-review face.
- **Cross-seat line (spec file on a `domain:server` card) — declared on the claim**, with no `domain:spec` seat live to consult; the member is one optional key on a contract the automation engine already owns the reading of. Nothing to add.
- **Outside the card, pre-existing, not owed here:** the reconstructed (no-journal) replay in `resolveRecordedContinuation` carries neither `resumedBy` nor `impersonatedBy`, as the dev's report notes; the `sys_comment` fork stays with the maintainer on #30213.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` — **holds.** Each break attempt, against the cited code:

- *A signal carrying `impersonatedBy` without the service marker* — `decider` is `undefined` at L326 and L327 returns the persisted context before the member is read; pinned (CONTROL, no marker).
- *A marker-carrying signal naming an administrator with no `resumedBy`* — same early return; the run keeps its identity and its own stamp; pinned (CONTROL, no decider).
- *A self-decider whose trigger-time context carried a stamp* — L334–340 returns a copy with the stamp removed when the decision carries none; pinned on both `runAs` arms (ablation A3 reds it).
- *An impersonated decider* — the switched segment carries the decision's administrator, the self-decider segment likewise; pinned on both arms, plus the trigger user deciding while impersonated (A4 reds it).
- *A second plain decision after an impersonated one* — the switched branch deletes the persisted stamp first; pinned.
- *A restored or replayed run after a restart* — two carriers: the persisted context at the next pause is the segment's (run-resume.ts re-suspend site), and a stranded decision's journal keeps `impersonatedBy` beside `resumedBy` (L5576), replayed by `continueRestoredRun` only beside a non-empty `resumedBy` and trimmed (L8061–8066); pinned end to end through `restoreConsumedSuspension` (A5, A6 red it). The recall journal (L5994) carries neither, correctly: a recall names no decider.
- *Forging through the body or a non-service path* — the decision route takes the body as `input` only and the context from `resolveExecCtx`; `decideAndResume` reads `context` alone; `ApprovalDecisionInput` has no such key and the whitelist drops it; pinned (an `impersonatedBy: 'forged'` input stamps nothing). The plugin-auth side is pinned on the real better-auth pipeline: an `/update-user` body key `impersonatedBy` is ignored and the engine sees the session's administrator.
- *Could it widen what a run may do?* No reader outside audit and provenance exists (① last bullet); the segment's grants are still seeded for `userId`, and the system arm still resolves no grant.

Findings:

- **should-fix** — `packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts` L102–110, the `RunDataContext.impersonatedBy` docblock still reads "The administrator who made the write that started this run". After this PR the decider's segment carries the decision's administrator instead, which the hit now promises; the prose of a cited carrier contradicts the hit. One sentence, no behaviour; follow-up or a rider on the next touch.
- nit, no action owed — the `AutomationContext.impersonatedBy` docblock's "An approval decision replaces it for the decider's segment" is scoped to a decider's segment and so stays true of an SLA auto-decision, which has none and keeps the run's stamp; the engine docblock says that explicitly.

No must-fix.

Check-runs on `b5edf8ea` at the time of writing: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint & Repo Gates, every Lint shard, Type Check · source gates, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards among them); none failed. Still running: Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not pre-empt them, and the landing waits for green.

PR #30874 · head `b5edf8ea` · 2026-11-06T08:16Z · card #30851 (follow-ups of PR #30800's contract review, records 6676544432 and 6677397495; ruling A on #30213) · claim re-posted with Branch `claude/project-thread-xv0lyn` and the widened surface · os-dev report 6680265453 · contract review PASS 6680400800 (`b5edf8ea`)

## 维护者速读（席位校正）

The body's six lines stand as written, read against the diff. The last line is now met: the contract review PASSed on this head. The claim's plan of two PRs became one: both items land here, with `Fixes #30851`.

## 席位核对

- **Card fit:** item 1: plugin-auth's identity-table writes made while an administrator impersonates a user carry `impersonatedBy`, read from the session, so `sys_audit_log.metadata.impersonated_by` names the administrator. Item 2: the decider's segment carries exactly the decision-time `impersonatedBy`. A self-decider's trigger-time stamp is dropped, an impersonated decider carries the administrator, and a plain decider carries none.
- **Route A (seat's implementation choice inside the card's Expected line):** one optional `ResumeSignal.impersonatedBy` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, a `domain:spec` file carried under the claim's cross-seat line. It is honoured only beside `resumedBy` under `RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE` (a `Symbol.for`, which no JSON body can carry). The approvals decide path reads it off the request context, never `input`. The journal and the restored continuation carry it beside `resumedBy`. The reviewer enumerated every non-test reader: none is an authorization reader, so the change is attribution-only.
- **Declarations:** `Fixes #30851`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (re-derived from the claim's provisional `no`: a new spec member, plugin-auth's `resolveAttributedActor` / `AttributedAuthActor`, and an optional `PlatformAdminActor.impersonatedBy`), `Metadata-protocol: none`, and one changeset with patch on four packages. The level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone (the no-major gate), so patch is right; Check Changeset is green.
- **Accepted deviations:** the `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` docblock in `engine.ts` (the contract of the body it changes) and plugin-auth files beyond the named ones, inside the claim's `plugin-auth/src/**`.
- **Carried, no card:** the `RunDataContext.impersonatedBy` docblock in `service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts` (L102–110) still reads "the write that started this run". It should also say the decider's segment. This is prose only, to fix on the next touch of that file (review should-fix). Outside this card: the reconstructed no-journal replay carries neither `resumedBy` nor `impersonatedBy` (pre-existing), and the `sys_comment` fork stays with the maintainer on #30213.
- **Overlap:** open PR #30717 edits `auth-manager.ts` / `auth-plugin.ts` in other hunks; the reviewer read them as textually disjoint.
- **Gates (report):** 88 derived, 88 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED; `pnpm lint`, `check:cli-command-ids` and `check:adr-symbol-anchors` 0. Suites: auth 4096, automation 3429, approvals 1502. Six ablations went red and were restored, one of them the repro on the real `/update-user` route.
- **Landing:** `check-governed-merges --pr 30874`: NOT governed, +484/-48. The seat lands with `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` once every check on `b5edf8ea` is green or expected-skip.
